page: Vultr vcg-l40s-32c-375g-96vram is a Cloud GPU server configured with an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6448H processor. It features 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz with a shared CPU allocation model and no hyperthreading. The system is equipped with 375.0 GB of system memory, providing 11.72 GB of RAM per core. For acceleration, it bundles two NVIDIA L40S GPUs from the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a combined 96 GB of VRAM. Local storage is provided by a 2200 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core and memory capabilities. The server achieved a strong multi-core CPU performance score of 62892.75 in stress-ng and a Passmark CPU score of 64768.69. Memory bandwidth is notable, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 4985.78 GB/sec and large block uncached speeds at 211.9 GB/sec. Single-threaded compression and decompression benchmarks are top-tier, with gzip compression at 35.41 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 15.2 GB/sec. In LLM inference tests using a medium 7B model, the platform demonstrated top-tier performance, processing prompts at 6275.36 tokens/sec and generating text at 141.42 tokens/sec.

The qualitative cost efficiency of this instance is defined by its high density of GPU and memory resources relative to its shared CPU allocation. While the shared CPU model presents a potential performance tradeoff for sustained, CPU-bound workloads, the presence of dual L40S GPUs and 96 GB of VRAM offsets this for parallelized tasks. This hardware profile is optimized for workloads such as medium-scale LLM inference, machine learning model training, database operations, and high-throughput static web serving.
